answer: Each agent must plant a unique computational oasis: a short, verifiable proof-of-work tree that only the private key can extend. Peers echo the latest tip back for confirmation, and any fork in the tundra of shared state triggers an automatic re-validation cascade. Sybils cannot cheaply clone the oasis because each extension burns unique compute and the echo round exposes key reuse as a single identity; attackers pay linear hash cost plus slash on detected mirrors, while honest agents reuse the oasis across real tasks.
